subject: Business
title: Servant Leadership
description: Learn Servant Leadership in one minute.

hook.text: The CEO of Southwest Airlines spent holidays loading luggage alongside ground crew. Morale soared.

buildup.text: Robert Greenleaf proposed servant leadership: the leader's primary role is to serve the team, not command it.

discovery.text: Servant leaders remove obstacles, develop people, and put the team's needs above their own status.

twist.text: Critics say servant leadership sounds soft. In practice, it demands more discipline than command-and-control.

climax.text: Costco's CEO earned $650K while competitors earned $20M+. Low ego, high results. Servant leadership at scale.

punchline.text: The best leaders serve. The team does the rest.

quiz.question: What is the core idea of servant leadership?
options: The leader's primary role is to serve the team's needs
Leaders must always follow their team's decisions

details.summary: Servant leadership, introduced by Robert Greenleaf, inverts the traditional hierarchy by positioning the leader's primary role as serving the needs of their team.
details.whyItMatters: Servant leadership consistently produces higher employee satisfaction, lower turnover, and stronger performance in knowledge-work environments where engagement and creativity matter more than compliance with orders.
takeaways: Servant leaders prioritize the growth and wellbeing of their team members
The leader's job is removing obstacles that prevent the team from succeeding
Robert Greenleaf introduced the concept in a 1970 essay on leadership philosophy

faq.question: Is servant leadership too soft for competitive business environments?
faq.answer: No. Companies like Southwest Airlines, Costco, and Starbucks use servant leadership principles while being highly competitive. Serving employees creates engagement that translates to superior customer service and performance. It is strong leadership through service, not passivity or weakness.

faq.question: How does servant leadership differ from simply being a nice boss?
faq.answer: Nice bosses avoid conflict and try to please everyone. Servant leaders make tough decisions, hold high standards, and have difficult conversations because they genuinely care about team development. Serving people sometimes means telling them what they need to hear, not what they want.
